{{Top|leg}}
[[File:PirateSpeederTank-SWE.png|thumb|right|250px|The WLO-5 speeder tank was classified as a heavy repulsortank]]
{{Quote|But you know what I always say: Speak softly and drive a big tank.|[[Hondo Ohnaka/Legends|Hondo Ohnaka]], on the WLO-5 speeder tank|<ref name="Bounty Hunters">{{TCW|Bounty Hunters (episode)}}</ref>}}
A '''heavy repulsortank''' was a classification of [[Hovertank/Legends|repulsortank]] used by the [[Imperial Army/Legends|Imperial Army]]. Equipped with the toughest armor and most powerful weapons available, heavy repulsortanks were generally considered to be a [[Squad/Legends|squad]]-level unit for deployment purposes. Their firepower rivalled that of stationary [[Artillery/Legends|artillery]] pieces, and they could take an enormous amount of punishment from other heavy assault vehicles.<ref name="J9">{{JournalCite|9|Repulsortank Battlefield}}</ref>

The [[Imperial Army/Legends|Imperial Army]] employed several variants of heavy repulsortanks, including the [[Gorm•Talquist]] [[S-1 FireHawke Heavy Repulsortank]],<ref name="Destiny">{{WEGCite|story=Hammer of Destiny|book=Imperial Entanglements (Star Wars Miniatures Battles)}}</ref> the [[Ubrikkian Industries/Legends|Ubrikkian Industries]] [[Imperial-class 1-H repulsortank/Legends|Imperial Repulsortank 1-H]],<ref name="J9" /> and a [[Imperial Heavy Repulsortank|model]] employed on [[Edan II/Legends|Edan II]].<ref name="Intro">''[[Introductory Adventure Game]]''</ref> Equipped with the same [[Taim & Bak/Legends|Taim & Bak]] [[MS-1 fire-linked heavy laser cannon/Legends|MS-1 fire-linked heavy laser cannon]] as the later Imperial [[All Terrain Armored Transport/Legends|All Terrain Armored Transport]], the [[Ubrikkian Ord Pedrovia/Legends|Ubrikkian Ord Pedrovia]] [[WLO-5 speeder tank/Legends|WLO-5 speeder tank]] was also classified as a heavy repulsortank.<ref name="The Gungan General Episode Guide">{{SW|url=series/clone-wars/the-gungan-general-episode-guide|text="The Gungan General" Episode Guide &#124; The Clone Wars}}</ref>
